featured_reviews.name: Neha Desai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Greenr Cafe in Breach Candy continues to be one of my favourite places in the city and my most recent visit only reaffirmed why. I took my best friend, who was in town, and we absolutely loved everything about the experience. The space is beautiful, the vibe is effortlessly relaxed, and every corner feels welcoming and thoughtfully designed.

Amongst the smoothie, falafel roll, ginger clear tea, we also ordered our favourite, the pesto spaghetti, as we always do. This time, however, it came out very dry and a little bitter, even after requesting the chef to make it a bit creamier. However, the team was responsive, and the server eventually had the order cancelled for us. I was a bit surprised that the chef seemed unable to adapt the dish to our request, but that was the only real hiccup in an otherwise lovely meal.

Overall, Greenr Cafe remains a favourite thanks to its beautiful ambience, great service, and consistently good food. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a vibrant, health-forward cafe with great energy.

featured_reviews.review_text: The place was amazing, love the vibe. The food was delicious and flavourful, customer service was so helpful and kind. Would definitely visit again.

featured_reviews.name: Cristina Harrell
featured_reviews.review_text: A vast menu of vegetarian and vegan friendly food for all to enjoy. Menu is a little confusing in that it ranged from sushi/asian flavours to burgers and beyond, but everything I ate was very tasty and well prepared. I particularly enjoyed the veg sushi options whereas I’m not sure if I would order some of the other dishes again (they were fine but not memorable). I’m keen to go back and try some more of the dishes, hopefully I can get there soon!

featured_reviews.review_text: Wow this place is fantastic. Really creative combinations of flavors. I’m not one to usually seek out vegetarian restaurants but I’ll be going back here.

featured_reviews.review_text:

This time we came in just for drinks and ordered smoothies and coffees all of them were pretty good. It is slightly pricey, but that seems to be the case with most cafés these days.

Overall, a reliable place with good-quality, healthy options.

featured_reviews.name: Utkarsh Dalal
featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Betterwithbffs
featured_reviews.review_text: We recently visited this newly opened cafe @iteeha.coffee store in Mahalaxmi. This place has an amazing soothing ambience and I’m totally in love with it. Not only the ambience is comforting but the food is so good that you’ll be wanting more. We tried their Mac & Cheese which was exactly perfect for the quote don’t judge a book by its cover😂 It looked a little sad but honestly it’s one of the best mac & cheese I’ve ever tasted. The second was the Ham and Cheese sandwich, this is the dish that stuck in my mind. It’s super yummy and even after a few days of visit I’m still craving for more. The next was Butter croissant, it was flaky, crispy and loaded with butter. Chicken Quiche was our next choice. The pastry was perfectly golden and crispy and it’s definitely a good one. For beverages, we tried their House cold coffee with Vanilla bean ice cream, it’s definitely a must try for all those who love thick coffee shake. We even tried their Mocha which was also amazing. The staff even managed to convince us to try their new Orange Chilli Hot Chocolate which was something I was hesitant but honestly it was so good. The hot chocolate had the perfect orange zest and chilli spice. Everything was so well balanced. For the desserts we had their New York Cheesecake and it’s definitely one of the best I’ve had yet. In all it’s just a place you’d want to spend an evening at with relaxing ambience and good food. The staff was amazing making our meal perfect.

featured_reviews.name: Tanishka Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
My recent visit at this cafe totally has my heart. With great food and service this place is just a spot to relax. The vibe of this place is so peaceful and the ambience is just great. With a great subtle decor this place is absolutely gorgeous. Every corner of this cafe is Instagram worthy. We were served by Lloyd and Sashikant. They both were attentive and the service was quick. They even made sure every table and every part of the cafe is maintained clean.
Few items mentioned below are which I gave a try and would recommend it to all.
• Affogato Vanilla Coffee :- Basically it's an Italian dessert with a scoop of vanilla ice cream over which an espresso is poured. This combination is absolutely amazing and is enjoyed by every coffee lover. You either sip on it or have it with a spoon. The taste is strong and would definitely recommend it to everyone.
• Vietnamese Cold Brew :- This coffee is made using sweetened condensed milk instead of milk, sugar or any sweetner. This does taste very different and is something which you need to give it a try.
• Veg Quiche:- Quiche is basically a custard baked in a flaky pie crust shell. It's stuffed with various options and is enjoyed by every one. Here we tried is the veg quiche which had cheese and leek.
• Chicken Quiche :- Similar to the up one, only difference is it has chicken stuffing.
• Ham & Cheese Sandwich:- This one absolutely had my heart. Super super delicious crisp sandwich. The classic sandwich which never fails to amaze you.
• Classic Chicken Sandwich :- Great great filling absolutely different than we usually get and would anyday go for this one. Chicken lovers, this crisp amazing delicious Sandwich is worth a try.
• Chocolate Cake :- One of the best chocolate cakes I have had. Soft, melting in mouth this cake has my heart.

This was my very first visit & experience to a pet-friendly restaurant and animal spa, and I must say it turned out to be a truly pleasant experience. The food quality ranges between average and good, depending on what you choose from the menu. What really sets this place apart, however, is its warm service and inviting ambience.

The staff impressed me with how naturally they interacted with dogs — they seemed fluent in “dog talk” and genuinely lived up to the brand’s promise. It felt like a space designed not just for owners to dine, but for dogs to feel at ease, play, and socialize. Meanwhile, owners could relax, chat, network, or simply enjoy the company of fellow dog lovers, all while their pets mingled happily inside the venue.

As for the food, the pasta stood out. The pesto was flavorful, and the shrimp were generously sized — a dish that definitely left a good impression.

featured_reviews.name: SUNIKET DANGE
featured_reviews.review_text:
As Mishri’s dad and someone who genuinely loves good food, Zane’s Café has become more than just a place. It’s an experience I keep coming back to, even after 3 years.

What truly sets this place apart is the vibe. It’s not just a pet café. It’s a space thoughtfully built for pets first, and humans are lucky to be a part of it. A true leash-free environment where Mishri can just be herself, roam around freely, socialize, and feel at home. And as a pet parent, that peace of mind is priceless.

Every single detail here feels intentional, from the layout to the energy. Everything is designed to make both pets and their humans comfortable. It’s rare to find a place that gets this balance so right.

Now coming to the food, which is the other big reason I keep returning. It never disappoints. Honestly, you could close your eyes, point at anything on the menu, and you will still end up with something delicious. Every dish is consistently well made and full of flavour.

And if there’s one thing you absolutely shouldn’t miss, it’s the Zane’s X Pallonji Cold Brew. It’s something that you’ll get only here.

Great food, amazing coffee, and a space where Mishri is just as happy as I am. That’s what keeps bringing us back. 🐾

featured_reviews.name: Monica
featured_reviews.review_text:
If South Mumbai’s cafe culture had to be summed up in one place, this would be it. Cafe Free India brings together great food, a lively setting, and an atmosphere that keeps you hooked from the moment you walk in.

The space carries a strong Goan inspired vibe, paired with an energy that feels vibrant and effortless. What truly sets it apart is the 📍Live Karaoke hosted Four Times a week ( Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun, 9pm onwards ) It adds a sense of excitement to the entire experience and makes the place feel dynamic and interactive.

The food here leans towards indulgent comfort. The parmesan corn ribs are juicy and full of flavour, while the honey chilli lotus root stands out with the perfect balance of sweet and spice. Their pizzas are rich, cheesy, and consistently satisfying.

The drinks menu keeps things interesting with beers on tap and cocktails inspired by iconic parts of Mumbai like the Sea Link. Seasonal additions like the mango chilli margarita bring in a refreshing twist.

When it comes to desserts, this is where you should absolutely give in. The gooey brownie with vanilla ice cream paired with an irresistible mango cream is easily one of the highlights and something you cannot go wrong with.

Overall, Cafe Free India in Lower Parel delivers more than just a meal. With its food, drinks, and high energy karaoke nights, it is a place that promises a fun and memorable outing.

featured_reviews.name: Ameeta mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
A charming little spot with proper coffee and big heart.

Lokoman Café isn't a trendy, flashy destination—it's a small, warm, and genuinely friendly neighbourhood spot where the focus is clearly on good coffee, simple homemade food, and a welcoming vibe.

The Atmosphere (5/5):
We loved the feel of it. It's compact and cozy, with a rustic, slightly vintage decor. Mismatched furniture, local art on the walls, and shelves with books and board games give it a real "living room" feel. There's a small, sunny terrace perfect for people-watching. The music was low-key, and the overall noise level lets you actually have a conversation.

Coffee & Food (4/5):
The coffee is the real deal. We had a flat white and a pour-over—both were expertly made, smooth, and rich. They clearly know their beans. We tried the "Lokoman Breakfast Plate" (eggs, sourdough, avocado, halloumi) and the Banana Bread. The food is fresh, wholesome, and tastes homemade. Portions are generous without being overwhelming. The banana bread, warm and moist, was a standout.

Service & Vibe:
The owner or manager (we assume) was behind the bar, and the service was exceptionally warm and personal. You get the sense this is a passion project, not a chain. It feels like a community hub; several patrons seemed to be regulars, greeted by name.

Things to Note:

It's small. On a busy weekend, you might wait for a table inside, but turnover seems reasonable.

The menu is compact—think all-day breakfast, sandwiches, salads, cakes, and stellar coffee. Don't expect a vast, sprawling menu.

It’s a place for slowing down. Perfect for a quiet catch-up, some reading, or getting a bit of work done in a pleasant environment.

Final Take:
Lokoman Café is a gem for those tired of impersonal, overpriced coffee shops. It’s authentic, unpretentious, and delivers exactly what it promises: excellent coffee, tasty comfort food, and a cozy atmosphere served with a sincere smile. We left feeling happily caffeinated and already planning our next visit. A wonderful local find.

Cafe Universal is well presented and in a convenient location, just a short walk from other bars and places to eat, which initially makes it appealing. However, after spending time there, it didn’t quite live up to expectations. Prices were noticeably higher compared to similar venues in Goa that we’d visited previously, and the value for money just wasn’t there.

My partner had been here around 20 years ago and remembered it as a lively backpacker bar with plenty of atmosphere and character. Sadly, that vibe seems to have been lost. Now it feels more like an expensive local bar, lacking the energy and buzz it once had.

While everything looked polished and tidy, it felt like style over substance, with nothing that really stood out or made us want to stay longer. Overall, it was an okay experience but not a memorable one, and we wouldn’t choose to return when there are better, more atmospheric options nearby.

This is the version you tell people about: hot keema—fine‑grain mutton, tomatoes, green chili—heaped on a plate with butter‑licked pav maska toasted till the edges crunch. Special Chai arrives in a huge glass, milky‑sweet with ginger bite, just enough to cut the fat. You break pav, drag it through keema, sip chai, repeat. featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
An unforgettable Thai brunch experience that truly transported us straight to the bustling streets of Bangkok 🇹🇭✨
We recently attended the Tuk Tuk Tales pop-up at Plate & Pint curated by the incredibly talented Chef Akanksha Saigal, and every single dish on the menu reflected her passion, creativity, and deep understanding of authentic Thai flavours.
We went as a group of friends for brunch, and honestly, it turned into one of those meals where every plate sparks conversation, every bite feels memorable, and time just flies by over great food and even better company. The vibe at Plate & Pint added so much warmth to the experience — lively, cozy, vibrant, and perfect for a long indulgent afternoon.
The meal began with the Mango & Avocado Ceviche — incredibly fresh, bright, and beautifully balanced with chilli, lime, cilantro, green apple, and crispy shallots adding layers of texture and zing. A refreshing start that instantly awakened the palate.
The Crispy Potato Stacks were an absolute standout. Perfectly crisp with rich green curry notes, aromatic fried basil, chilli crackling, and toasted herb rice bringing together comfort and complexity in every bite.
The Gai Yang Thai BBQ Chicken was beautifully charred and deeply flavourful, paired wonderfully with pickled cucumber, pickled chilli, and a delicious dipping sauce that elevated the smokiness of the chicken.
The Spicy Tamarind Glaze dishes were another highlight. Both the cottage cheese and pork belly versions were packed with bold sweet spicy flavours and had that addictive Thai style balance that keeps you reaching for another bite.
For mains, the Holy Basil Stir Fry was pure comfort food done right. Fragrant basil, juicy chicken, cucumber, fluffy rice, and a fried egg made this dish hearty, satisfying, and incredibly soulful.
The Tom Yum Hot Pot was bursting with authentic Thai aromatics — lemongrass, galangal, lime leaf — with the prawns soaking beautifully in the deeply comforting broth. Warm, sharp, spicy, and layered with flavour.
And of course, no Thai meal feels complete without a great Pad Thai, and this one absolutely delivered. Perfectly cooked rice noodles coated in tamarind sauce with chicken, bean sprouts, and peanuts creating the ideal balance of sweet, savoury, nutty, and tangy flavours.
Dessert was the perfect finale — Mango Sticky Rice with tender coconut ice cream. Rich, fragrant, comforting, and tropical all at once. Easily one of the best versions we’ve had in Mumbai.
The cocktails were equally thoughtful and fun, especially the Thai Chilli Guava Michelada and Mango Chilli White Wine Spritz, which paired beautifully with the food and added another vibrant layer to the entire experience.
Huge compliments to Chef Akanksha for creating such a well executed pop-up that didn’t just serve food, but genuinely told a story through flavours. Every dish felt curated with heart and authenticity.
Thank you for inviting us and giving us such a memorable afternoon filled with laughter, amazing conversations, delicious food, and beautiful hospitality. Experiences like these are exactly why food brings people together so effortlessly.

Already looking forward to the next one ❤️

featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Paradise offers a pleasant ambiance with good service, including options for AC and non-AC seating as well as a family hall, making it a convenient choice for different group types. The staff are courteous and attentive, contributing to a positive dining experience. However, there are notable concerns about the food quality, particularly with the egg fried rice, which did not meet expectations.

The egg fried rice ordered contained chicken, which was unexpected and suggests either a mistake or a less conventional preparation. In authentic Chinese cuisine, egg fried rice usually does not include meat unless specified. Moreover, the use of spices like cardamom and cinnamon in the fried rice is unusual for traditional Chinese recipes. These spices are more commonly found in South Asian dishes like biryanis and can result in a dry texture and flavor profile that is quite different from the typical savory and umami taste expected from Chinese fried rice. This deviation likely contributed to the dissatisfaction with the dish.

Additionally, the drink options were limited. The Goli soda offered, while a unique choice, had an inconvenient cap design that made drinking awkward, detracting further from the overall dining experience.

To summarize, while the ambiance and service at Cafe Paradise are commendable—with comfortable seating and friendly staff—the food quality, specifically the egg fried rice, could be improved to better align with authentic Chinese flavors. The unusual use of spices like cardamom and cinnamon, along with the unexpected chicken addition, resulted in a dish that was dry and lacked the typical taste profile. The drink selection also needs enhancement for a better customer experience. Improvements in menu authenticity and drink variety could make Cafe Paradise a more satisfying dining destination

featured_reviews.name: Debie Morera
featured_reviews.review_text:
Barista Cafe Urmi Axis is the kind of place that does exactly what you need it to. Located in the same building as VFS, it’s an especially convenient stop for people waiting for their appointments. You’ll often find a steady flow of visitors coming in to pass the time, grab a quick drink, or settle their nerves before paperwork and interviews.
The cafe leans more toward practicality than ambiance, but that’s not necessarily a bad thing. It offers a comfortable enough space to sit, recharge, and take a break from the formal setting downstairs. The coffee is reliable, and the menu covers the basics well—nothing overly elaborate, but enough to keep you satisfied while you wait.
Service is generally quick, which fits the needs of its crowd. People aren’t usually there to linger for hours, and the staff seems to understand that rhythm.
Overall, Barista Cafe Urmi Axis works best as a functional, convenient pit stop. It may not be a destination cafe, but for anyone heading to VFS, it’s a handy and dependable place to spend some time.

featured_reviews.name: Anusha Sundaram
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you don't do something right, don't do it at all - The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf should consider taking up this motto.

Openly located inside the Skyzone shopping area of High Street Phoenix, this location is rather loud and, sadly, abundant in flies. The plus side of this place is that it gives your tired feet some solace as you rest your piggies in between shopping sprees.

We ordered the Hazelnut Tiramisu and Three-Layered Chocolate Mousse. We were less than impressed by both. The tiramisu is wrongly named. It is in no way similar to the delectable Italian dessert. The cake was dry, there was no taste of espresso, and it surely had no hint of mascarpone cheese. The white layer of the mousse was extremely grainy and the overall dish was a let down.

Service is quick and you pay at the register. They have employees who clean the tables promptly.

It is a suggestion that this café stick to drinks as their dessert game is subpar.
